messages:
Maya: Heads-up — saw a recurring latency spike during yesterday's EU burst window. p99 jumped from ~120ms to ~880ms for multiple sandy replicas. Traces point at a kernel-selection loop and a spike in KV cache cold misses.

Ravi: Thanks Maya — linking traces: https://perf.redwood/traces/shot/abcd1234 :eyes: Also observed provisioning queue depth increase around the same time.

Tim: Can you paste the profiler snippet? I suspect batching heuristic is oscillating and flipping kernel choices every few requests.

Maya: Paste from the sampler:
```
kernel_selector: scored candidates [int8_qkv, fp16_opt, fp16_fused]
selected: fp16_opt -> exec 12.1ms
next_req: selected int8_qkv -> exec 30.3ms
selection_delta_ms: 18.2
kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.37
warm_pool_occupancy: 0.42
```

Sasha: That KV miss rate jump (0.06 -> 0.37) matches what I saw in the metrics. Warm pool occupancy dropped ~60% during the spike window. Looks like warm forks weren't compatible with the alternate kernel path, causing re-warm and eviction thrash.

Ken: Hypothesis: kernel selector churn -> incompatible warm forks -> repeated KV prefetch/cold loads -> autoscaler perceives slow responses and spins up replicas -> new replicas also suffer cold KV misses -> a feedback loop. Noisy neighbor effect exacerbates kernel perf variance.

perf-bot: perf alert: 1918399800 - kernel-selection-churn detected (anomaly score 7.8). Attached metric snapshots to the alert.

Ravi: Quick repro steps that exposed the oscillation:
```
loadtest --target sandy --qps 250 --seq-len 64 --duration 5m
```
Oscillation typically starts ~45s into the run and stabilizes if we force a single kernel.

Tim: Proposed quick mitigations to try on canary: add hysteresis to kernel selection and raise batching hold to give batches more time to stabilize. Example patch:
```
runtime.kernel_selection.stability_window_ms = 2000
runtime.kernel_selection.min_switch_delta_ms = 15
runtime.batching.min_batch_hold_ms = 6
```
Pin initial kernel for warm forks to avoid incompatible cold starts.

Maya: Rolled the canary this morning at 07:40 UTC with those three tweaks. Early numbers: p95 back to ~140ms, p99 down to ~220ms. Token throughput down ~4%, but latency tail improved significantly.

Sasha: Follow-ups: implement explicit KV prefetch on warmpool handoff and increase warm pool target fill by +20% during burst windows. Also add a guard metric for "kernel_churn_count" so autoscaler can ignore transients.

Ken: Filed GH issue #3245: "kernel selector: introduce hysteresis and warm-fork compatibility map" with perf traces and repro steps.

Tim: Plan of action: (1) keep canary config for 24h, (2) add KV prefetch change and run a second canary, (3) add kernel_churn metric + autoscaler filter, (4) if it reoccurs open a postmortem and consider warmpool sizing change.

Maya: I'll monitor dashboards and signal if anything regresses. Will also attach the full profiler dump to the GH issue. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: scheduled incident watch for 24h (owner: Maya)

Ravi: Quick note — if canary stabilizes, we should backport the hysteresis change to dedicated and private branches after QA.

Maya: Ack. Will keep thread updated with SLO/throughput delta and warm pool occupancy numbers.

Sasha: Adding one more data point — when we forced `kernel_selector.force=fp16_opt` in the loadtest, warm pool occupancy stayed >0.9 and p99 settled ~130ms. That reinforces the warm-fork compatibility theory.

Ken: Good. If this holds we can ship hysteresis + warm-fork pin as a targeted mitigation while we work on a longer-term compatibility map and smarter batching heuristics.

Maya: Closing interim loop — monitoring continuing. I'll post final results in 24h. :white_check_mark:
